questions.question:
**Directions:** Below a question is given with two statements (I) and (II). These statements may be either independent causes or may be effects of independent causes or a common cause. One of these statements may be the effect of the other statement. Read both the statements and decide which of the following answer choice correctly depicts the relationship between these two statements.

**(A)** There was a long power cut in the Karol bagh.

**(B)** The municipality was repairing the power grid of Karol bagh.

options.text: Statement (A) is the cause and statement (B) is its effect
Statement (B) is the cause and statement (A) is its effect
Both statements (A) and (B) are independent causes
Both statements (A) and (B) are effects of independent causes

questions.solution:
A long power cut was experienced in Karol bagh due to the repair work at power grid.

Therefore, Statement (B) is the cause of the power cut and Statement (A) is the effect.

Hence, Statement (B) is the cause and statement (A) is its effect

questions.question: In a class, four students ranked between Rahul and Sreeja. Sreeja ranked 14th from the top while Rahul ranked 7th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution:
Given:

1) F**our students ranked between Rahul and Sreeja. Sreeja ranked 14th from the top while Rahul ranked 7th from the bottom.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/949cb9563323186b7070d30bf89a602b51af9923d58df953acd380cf24522308.png] 

2) Total number of students

=> Total number students = Sreeja's rank from top + Rahul's rank from bottom + students between Rahul and Sreeja

=> Total number students = 14 + 7 + 4 = 25

Hence, there are “25” students in the class.

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Rights are Places.

No Place is Big.

No Big is Bazaar.

**Conclusions:**

I. All Bazaar can never be Rights.

II. At least some Places are Bazaar.

III. Some Big can be Rights.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Both conclusions I and III follow
All conclusions I, II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73073d4f9df0aa26c51a86ad55b23ed4bd520b3eba02086e092847a0a249b706.png] 

**For Conclusions:**

I. All Bazaar can never be Right → False (There is no direct negative relationship given between Bazaar and Rights)

II. At least some Places are Bazaar → False (It is a possibility but not definite. Therefore, we can not say definitely about it)

III. Some Big can be Rights → True (This is a case of possibility which is true, which is shown in the below given diagram)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d7b9d672b3d42142d546f1db0a924aec35113a0e60939842b669e1b3fb46c2a.png] 

Hence, **Only conclusion III follows** is correct.

Thus, according to the final arrangement E sits to the extreme left.

Hence, **"E"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statement.

**Statement:**

All animals are lion.

Some animals are camel.

No camel is deer.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some animal are deer.

(II) No animal is deer.

(III) No deer are lion.
questions.solution:
Statement:

All animals are lion.

Some animals are camel.

No camel is deer.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47c2e77aca659727a63ccb820a761b8d18bcbef75b7c78789184526e92aad67a.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some animal are deer.→ False (Because there is no direct relation between 'animal ' and 'deer', so it is possible but not definite)

(II) No animal is deer. → False (Because there is no direct relation between 'animal ' and 'deer', so it is possible but not definite)

(III) No deer are lion. → False (Because there is no direct relation between 'deer' and 'lion', so it is possible but not definite)

Conclusion I and II form a complementary pair and both of them are false. Thus, this is the case of either and or.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Either I or II follows ".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Conditions of "Either nd or" Case 

 
• The conclusions should have complementary pair.
 
• Both conclusions should be false.
 
• The conclusion should be in 'Some and No' form or 'All and Some not'.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 —- Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 

(5, 2, 121)

(4, 3, 55)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is, 

Logic:** Third Number = (First Number)³ - (Second Number)²**

**(5, 2, 121)**

→ 121 = (5)³ - (2)²

→ 121 = 125 - 4

**(4, 3, 55)**

→ 55 = (4)3 - (3)2

→ 55 = 64 - 9

Let's check each option,

1) **(2, 8, 67)**

→ 67 = (2)3 - (8)2

→ 67 ≠ 8 - 64

2) **(4, 2, 60)**

→ 60 = (4)3 - (2)2

→ 60 = 64 - 4 ⇒ **Satisfies the logic.**

3)** (6, 8, 91)**

→ 91 = (6)3 - (8)2

→ 91 ≠ 216 - 64

4) **(3, 1, 9)**

→ 9 = (3)3 - (1)2

→ 9 ≠ 27 - 1

Here, we can see that only Option 2 satisfies the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **"****(4, 2, 60)"**.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

9 : 90 :: 15 : ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

**Let (1st number : 2nd number)**

**1st number × (1****st ****number + 1) = 2nd number**

Now follow the steps:

9 : 90

=> 9 × (9 + 1) = 9 × 10 = 90 = 2nd number

Similarly,

**15 : ?**

**=> 15 × (15 + 1) = 15 × 16 = 240 = 2nd number**

Hence, **"240"** is correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The pattern followed here is,

**Let (1st number : 2nd number)**

**(1st number)² + 1st number = 2nd number**

Now follow the steps:

9 : 90

=> 9² + 9 = 81 + 9 = 90 = 2nd number

Similarly,

**15 : ?**

**=> 15² + 15 = 225 + 15 = 240 = 2nd number**

Hence, **"240"** is correct answer.
